rationale: The n-body benchmark is a tiny, hot floating-point simulation loop (advance/offset routines called ~10^6+ times per run) with no source-level metadata available, so the table prioritizes passes whose transformations survive in tight numeric loops while penalizing those whose per-iteration overhead dominates: BCF and FLA get high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so they are applied selectively (stub-only or to non-inner-loop functions) rather than blanket-applied to the hot kernel, since bogus predicates and dispatcher switches can double runtime of FP loops; FLA also carries a moderate CorrectnessRisk weight because flattening loop-carried FP control flow can perturb value-optimization opportunities. SUB is favored strongly (low runtime/size/correctness penalties, high diversity gain) because arithmetic substitutions are cheap and obscure the physics constants' algebra, and IGV is enabled with moderate penalties since global variable indirection hides the orbital-parameter dataflow at low loop cost; IBR gets mid-range weights (useful jump-chain obfuscation but non-trivial branch cost in hot code), and ICALL is weighted cautiously with a higher CorrectnessRisk because indirect-call rewriting of what are direct internal calls in this single-TU numeric code yields modest security benefit against potential FP-state and call-graph-analysis regressions; SPLIT stays enabled with low costs as a safe baseline diversity pass.
